reviewer: Claude coordinator and independent Claude review agents (text, illustrations)
text: Independent review agent read the full text against Ryder's King Joy and Secretary Splendor (Book IV); every beat is kept: the king's glory, the learned minister, both quarrels and both wives' terms, the next-morning council and its verse, and the monkey's rebuke with the parrot, heron and tiger-skin donkey.
Frame correct: the monkey tells it to the crocodile right after The Ungrateful Wife, reciting the verse first; Joy and Splendor become ನಂದ and ವರರುಚಿ, the Sanskrit names, disclosed.
The wives are playful and forgiving; the closing moral blames thoughtless obedience, not women, and Ryder's 'henpecked' is dropped and disclosed. No reason is invented for either quarrel.

Age 8+: nobody is hurt; only the crocodile's earlier plan and the donkey being caught are recalled. Review fixes applied: a throne misplaced in the queen's room, the neigh spelling, two repeated asides and the monkey's closing line. No em dashes.
illustrations: Storyboard 1024x1536, 403 KB; seams exactly on the 512 px grid; painted to every edge, no text.
King, minister and queen keep the same faces and clothes; the minister is bald from panel 2 with no tuft; an edit pass removed red forehead dots from the men in every panel.

After review, a second edit replaced a wall picture that read as a deity icon (panel 2) with a peacock painting, and a glass-paned door with guard silhouettes (panel 4) with a solid carved wooden door, matching the text that nobody saw.
Panel 4 is playful and fully clothed; the credit line truthfully states one generation, two edit passes, per-panel refit onto the grid and which panels were composited.
limitations: AI-agent editorial review, not human Kannada-teacher or scholar certification.
Age bands are editorial judgements against the README table and have not been tested with children, parents or adult readers.
Source fidelity was checked against saved copies of the Wikisource pages of Ryder's 1925 translation, not against Durgasimha's Kannada text or a Sanskrit recension.
Art was generated with Codex CLI on gpt-5.6-sol and judged on the full sheet and 512px panel crops with the grid measured in pixels; edited panels were re-checked by the same independent agent.
